messages.subject: Machine learning toolkit for predicting disease-associated genetic variants
messages.subject_clean: Machine learning toolkit for predicting disease-associated genetic variants
messages.body_plain:
Background

Due to the crucial role of genetic variants in disease onset, it is important to identify these disease-associated genetic variants accurately. However, there is no such R package available. In this GSOC project, we will invite students to tackle this problem by developing a machine learning toolkit consisting of two core novel machine learning algorithms to predict disease-associated genetic variants.

 <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2020/wiki/Machine-learning-toolkit-for-predicting-disease-associated-genetic-variants#details-of-your-coding-project>Details of your coding project

The purpose of this work is to provide R users with a comprehensive machine learning toolkit for predicting disease-associated genetic variants. It mainly consists of two core novel machine learning algorithms:
A weighted ensemble learning framework for predicting disease-associated genetic variants: The model will ensemble multiple score systems for predicting disease-associated genetic variants in a unified framework by developing a constrained penalized optimization algorithm.
A transfer learning framework based on convolutional neural network (CNN): The CNN is powerful when the sample size for a specific disease is small. In this case, CNN will be trained on an experiment-validated large-scale genetic variants from mixed diseases and fine-tuned using disease-specific genetic variants.

messages.subject: Reminders?
messages.body_plain:
I just took a look through the proposals to R for GSOC2020.

1) many project don't yet have comments
2) many don't have a mentor assigned
3) April 21 is not far away

For information of those on this gsoc-r group, I receive (along with a couple of other folk)
the requests to join the group. If the request does not identify in some way how the applicant
is associated with R, I ignore it. This can mean I'm blocking possible mentors, so do share
with those who may want to mentor that they should include a note "Wish to mentor (name of
project)" or something like that. Even better, let us know a tiny bit about yourself e.g.,
"prof at U of X". If the request interface fails, then email me at the above address.

We don't want projects to fail on technicalities like no mentor assigned.

Best,

John Nash
U of Ottawa (retired)

messages.subject: Updates for GSoC 2020 Mentors
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

Requesting all the GSoC 2020 Mentors to login to GSoC Dashboard [If you face any issue, reply on this thread or contact me immediately] and do the following:

1. Leave a comment on the [could be multiple] proposal[s] received against your project indicating your interests and short review of the submission.

2. This needs to be done by at least two mentors of that proposal, otherwise, that would be ignored during consideration.

3. Click on "Want to Mentor" this project, indicating interest against that student application. Same, minimum of two mentors against a submission. [1]

Thank you again for the hard work and now the real projects coming your way this summer.

Deadline: 19th April 2020

1. Button Snapshot for reference:

[on the left side of the proposal page]

Thanks,
Vivek

messages.body_plain:
It looks like a relatively large number of mentors have not commented on proposals.

I will go through things in the morning and invite any listed mentors who are not already invited to the summerofcode website.

If you are a mentor and have not commented on your proposal(s), please do so ASAP, as slot requests are due early next week.

If you intend to be a mentor and have not been invited, please contact the org admins.

Regards,

Brian
